text: Atypical depression is characterized by mood reactivity (improvement in mood in response to positive events) combined with features such as hyperphagia, hypersomnia, leaden paralysis, and a longstanding sensitivity to interpersonal rejection ( 1 ). Metabolically, it tends to co-occur with weight gain, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and elevated inflammatory markers like C-reactive protein and pro-inflammatory cytokines ( 2 , 3 ). Traditional treatments—psychopharmacology and psychotherapy—often fall short in fully remediating these underlying metabolic or immuno-inflammatory drivers ( 4 ).
source_label: Chrononutrition interventions for mental health: addressing atypical depression, ultra-processed food use disorder, and circadian dysregulation
